lead: Meta Platforms / FB — the biggest wipeout ever, bargain or trap
smaller: Amazon / AMZN — the giant that answered with AWS
3x Nasdaq 100 ETF / TQQQ — the leveraged dip-buy snaps back
Bitcoin / BTC — the faithful hold while Big Tech bleeds
why_lead: Repeat lead justified as a material update of the 2022-02-03 Meta lead ('the metaverse bill comes due'), which could cite only the after-hours reaction and named the 3 February regular session as the pending test. That session is now on the card (META 237.76 USD, -26.39% 1-session, -26.66% 20-session) and a large body of newly published 3 February evidence changes the story from after-hours shock to completed record wipeout: biggest one-day drop ever (CNBC n0811), $232 billion record (CNBC n1141) vs $251 billion (Bloomberg n0838), first-ever user shrink (n1142), $10 billion Apple sting (WSJ n1137), TikTok competition (n1166), world tech contagion (n0842), $1 trillion of funds exposed (Bloomberg n0837), Zuckerberg -$31 billion (n0834), Meta below Berkshire (n0841), Buffett ruling out buying (n0877), and the Big Tech divide framing (n1153, n0809). The angle is new — bargain or value trap at record scale, with PayPal's post-record further slide (n0733; card -6.24%) as the analog — and none of the 2022-02-03 lead's citations or wording is reused. Relation to other strictly earlier notes: 2022-02-01 GameStop and 2022-02-02 Alphabet leads are not repeated; PayPal (2022-02-02 and 2022-02-03 smaller) appears only as the Historical Analog with new card data.
why_smaller: Amazon / AMZN: new item, distinct pricing-power/cloud narrative — -7.81% to 2,776.91 USD in the 3 February session, then after-hours surge on the AWS beat and Rivian gain (CNBC n0787), AWS +40% to $17.78 billion (n0099), profit nearly doubling to $14.3 billion (n0785), Prime up nearly 17% to $139 (n0784); breaks on GeekWire's $1.8 billion ex-AWS operating loss (n0788) and the pending 4 February session.

3x Nasdaq 100 ETF / TQQQ: new item, distinct leverage narrative — TQQQ -12.03% to 56.74 USD and SOXL -13.60% as the Nasdaq 100 fell 4.22% (chipmakers tumbling on Qualcomm's high bar, n0796), still +10.05% over five sessions; daily-reset decay shown by -24.02% vs -8.06% for the index over 20 sessions; The Edge Singapore's house-always-wins headline (n0836).

Bitcoin / BTC: new item, distinct crypto-faith/decoupling narrative — bitcoin +0.55% to 37,154.60 USD and ether -0.14% on the day the Nasdaq 100 fell 4.22%; Stocktwits rolling out crypto trading (n1762) as retail-platform evidence, 'Bitcoin a religion' (n0966), the Wormhole hack ($325 million, Elliptic n0943) and Jump Crypto's bailout (n0962); breaks on the -13.79% 20-session gap, bailout dependence and Texas grid exposure (n0791).
considered_not_chosen: Spotify / SPOT (-16.76% to 159.76 USD after results; BBC n1916, Tubefilter n0867): would be a third consecutive appearance (2022-02-01, 2022-02-03 smaller items); the 3 February item's stated break (apology rebound as a bull trap) played out, but a third essay would recycle the story.

Snap / SNAP (-23.60% to 24.50 USD) and Pinterest / PINS (-10.32%; 'results dazzle Wall St' n0856 vs sliding active users n1156): used as contagion data in the lead; Snap's own results are covered only by an uninformative TechCrunch headline (n1161), and Pinterest's 'sold with Meta, then beat' story duplicates the Amazon item's narrative.
Ford / F (-3.59%; shares skid despite bullish outlook n0814; Rivian-boosted $17.9 billion n0813): the Rivian mark-to-market angle is covered in the Amazon item.
Digital World Acquisition / DWAC (+22.07% 5-session, +60.99% 20-session) and Robinhood (+21.88% 5-session): no own-date headline explaining the moves.

Pending after the cutoff and not treated as outcomes: US January payrolls (4 February 13:30 UTC; referenced only via the White House warning n2022), the Putin–Xi meeting and Beijing Olympic opening, the RBA Statement on Monetary Policy, and Amazon's 4 February regular session.
Feb 3-stamped items were checked for after-cutoff content; all cited ones describe 3 February sessions, after-hours results or decisions completed before 00:00 UTC on 4 February.
